sentences.en: Our dining table is big and new.

note: 'Meja tulis' means a writing desk or study table; 'meja' alone means any table, so context matters; related: 'meja makan' (dining table), 'kursi' (chair).

sentences.text: Buku saya ada di meja tulis.
sentences.en: My book is on the desk.

sentences.text: Dia belajar di meja tulis setiap hari.
sentences.en: She studies at the desk every day.

sentences.text: Meja tulis ini baru dan bersih.
sentences.en: This desk is new and clean.

english: indeed, yes I agree, that's absolutely right
note: 'Memang' is used to confirm or agree with something already known; more emphatic than 'ya', common in casual speech, similar to 'indeed' or 'that's just how it is'.

sentences.text: Makanan ini memang enak sekali.
sentences.en: This food is indeed very delicious.

sentences.text: Bali memang indah dan ramai.
sentences.en: Bali is indeed beautiful and busy.

sentences.text: Dia memang pandai berbicara bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: She is indeed good at speaking Indonesian.

note: 'Mencari' is the formal/written form; 'cari' is the casual spoken form — both mean 'to look for'; commonly confused with 'menemukan' which means 'to find'.

sentences.text: Saya mencari kunci saya di kamar.
sentences.en: I am looking for my key in the room.

sentences.text: Dia cari makanan enak di pasar.
sentences.en: She is looking for delicious food at the market.

sentences.text: Kami mencari hotel murah di Bali.
sentences.en: We are looking for a cheap hotel in Bali.

note: "Pot bunga" is everyday neutral Indonesian for a flower pot; also called "vas bunga" for a vase, but pot bunga typically sits on the floor or ground.

sentences.text: Ibu meletakkan bunga di pot bunga.
sentences.en: Mother places flowers in the flower pot.

sentences.text: Pot bunga itu ada di teras.
sentences.en: That flower pot is on the porch.

sentences.text: Kami membeli pot bunga baru kemarin.
sentences.en: We bought a new flower pot yesterday.

note: 'Radio' is the same in Indonesian and English; it refers to a radio device or broadcast, commonly used in everyday speech across all registers.

sentences.text: Ayah mendengarkan radio setiap pagi.
sentences.en: Father listens to the radio every morning.

sentences.text: Radio itu berbunyi keras sekali.
sentences.en: That radio is very loud.

sentences.text: Kami mendengar berita dari radio.
sentences.en: We heard the news from the radio.

note: 'Rak buku' is the everyday term for bookshelf or bookcase; 'rak' alone means shelf, and can combine with other words like 'rak sepatu' (shoe rack).

sentences.text: Buku itu ada di rak buku.
sentences.en: That book is on the bookshelf.

sentences.text: Saya meletakkan buku di rak buku.
sentences.en: I put the book on the bookshelf.

sentences.text: Rak buku ini penuh dengan buku.
sentences.en: This bookshelf is full of books.

note: "Rumah tangga" means household or domestic life; often used in phrases like "peralatan rumah tangga" (household items); distinct from "rumah" (house/building) alone.

sentences.text: Ibu mengurus rumah tangga setiap hari.
sentences.en: Mother takes care of the household every day.

sentences.text: Peralatan rumah tangga kami sudah tua.
sentences.en: Our household appliances are already old.

sentences.text: Ayah membantu pekerjaan rumah tangga juga.
sentences.en: Father also helps with household chores.

note: 'Televisi' (often shortened to 'TV' in casual speech) is the standard word for a television set; avoid confusing it with 'radio' (audio only).

sentences.text: Saya menonton televisi di rumah.
sentences.en: I watch television at home.

sentences.text: Televisi itu besar dan bagus.
sentences.en: That television is big and nice.

sentences.text: Anak-anak suka menonton televisi setiap hari.
sentences.en: Children like to watch television every day.

note: 'Tempat tidur' literally means 'sleeping place'; common in everyday speech, related words: 'kasur' (mattress), 'kamar tidur' (bedroom).

sentences.text: Tempat tidur saya ada di kamar.
sentences.en: My bed is in the room.

sentences.text: Dia tidur di tempat tidur besar.
sentences.en: He sleeps on a big bed.

sentences.text: Tempat tidur ini sangat nyaman.
sentences.en: This bed is very comfortable.

note: 'Biru' means blue and is used like an adjective after the noun it describes (e.g. baju biru = blue shirt); not to be confused with 'hijau' (green) or 'ungu' (purple).

sentences.text: Langit hari ini sangat biru.
sentences.en: The sky today is very blue.

sentences.text: Saya suka baju biru itu.
sentences.en: I like that blue shirt.

sentences.text: Mobilnya berwarna biru muda.
sentences.en: The car is light blue.

note: "Berwarna" means 'to be coloured' or 'colourful'; it is used before or after a noun, e.g. "baju berwarna merah" (a red-coloured shirt); related: "warna" (colour), "berwarna-warni" (multicoloured).

sentences.text: Baju itu berwarna merah dan putih.
sentences.en: That shirt is red and white in colour.

sentences.text: Bunga di taman berwarna kuning.
sentences.en: The flowers in the garden are yellow in colour.

sentences.text: Tas saya berwarna biru muda.
sentences.en: My bag is light blue in colour.

note: 'Berbicara' means 'to speak/talk' and is slightly more formal than 'ngomong'; often used with 'dengan' (with) or 'tentang' (about).

sentences.text: Saya berbicara dengan teman saya hari ini.
sentences.en: I am talking with my friend today.

sentences.text: Dia berbicara bahasa Indonesia dengan baik.
sentences.en: She speaks Indonesian well.

sentences.text: Kami berbicara tentang liburan di Bali.
sentences.en: We talked about the holiday in Bali.

english: an interior wall, a dividing, wall (in a house)
note: "Dinding" refers to interior or dividing walls inside a building; use "tembok" for thick exterior or concrete walls, and "pagar" for fences.

sentences.text: Ada foto keluarga di dinding itu.
sentences.en: There is a family photo on that wall.

sentences.text: Warna dinding kamarku adalah putih.
sentences.en: The color of my room's wall is white.

sentences.text: Anak itu menempel gambar di dinding.
sentences.en: That child is sticking a picture on the wall.

english: under, underneath, at the foot of
note: 'Di bawah' means 'under/below/underneath'; often confused with 'di atas' (above); used for physical position and abstract hierarchy

sentences.text: Kucing itu tidur di bawah meja.
sentences.en: The cat is sleeping under the table.

sentences.text: Sandal saya ada di bawah kursi.
sentences.en: My sandals are under the chair.

sentences.text: Anak itu duduk di bawah pohon.
sentences.en: The child is sitting under the tree.

note: 'Di atas' means 'above/on top of' and is always written as two words; don't confuse with 'di bawah' (below) or 'di dalam' (inside).

sentences.text: Buku itu ada di atas meja.
sentences.en: The book is on top of the table.

sentences.text: Kucing tidur di atas kursi.
sentences.en: The cat sleeps on top of the chair.

sentences.text: Burung terbang di atas pantai.
sentences.en: The bird flies above the beach.

note: 'Halo' is an informal, friendly greeting used at any time of day; similar to English 'hello' and also used when answering the phone.

sentences.text: Halo, nama saya Budi.
sentences.en: Hello, my name is Budi.

sentences.text: Halo, apa kabar hari ini?
sentences.en: Hello, how are you today?

sentences.text: Halo, selamat datang di Bali!
sentences.en: Hello, welcome to Bali!

note: 'Hijau' means green; commonly used for nature, traffic lights, and vegetables; related: 'daun hijau' (green leaf), 'lampu hijau' (green light).

sentences.text: Lampu hijau berarti kamu boleh jalan.
sentences.en: A green light means you can go.

sentences.text: Sayuran hijau itu sangat sehat.
sentences.en: Those green vegetables are very healthy.

sentences.text: Pohon di taman itu berwarna hijau.
sentences.en: The trees in the park are green.

note: "Hitam" means black or dark-coloured; commonly paired with nouns like "kucing hitam" (black cat) or "kopi hitam" (black coffee); opposite is "putih" (white).

sentences.text: Kucing itu berwarna hitam dan putih.
sentences.en: That cat is black and white.

sentences.text: Saya suka minum kopi hitam setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I like to drink black coffee every morning.

sentences.text: Tas saya berwarna hitam.
sentences.en: My bag is black.

english: a mobile phone, a hand phone
note: 'HP' (from 'handphone') is the everyday Indonesian term for a mobile phone; more formal is 'ponsel', but 'HP' is used in nearly all casual speech.

sentences.text: HP saya hilang di pasar tadi.
sentences.en: My phone got lost at the market earlier.

sentences.text: Boleh saya pinjam HP kamu?
sentences.en: May I borrow your phone?

sentences.text: Dia selalu main HP di kelas.
sentences.en: He always plays on his phone in class.

note: 'Guling' is a long cylindrical bolster pillow common in Indonesian homes; not to be confused with 'bantal' (square/rectangular pillow); also used in the phrase 'ayam guling' (spit-roasted chicken).

sentences.text: Saya tidur dengan guling setiap malam.
sentences.en: I sleep with a bolster every night.

sentences.text: Guling ini sangat empuk dan nyaman.
sentences.en: This bolster is very soft and comfortable.

sentences.text: Adik memeluk guling saat tidur siang.
sentences.en: My little sibling hugs the bolster when napping.

note: "Kanan" means the direction 'right' (opposite of 'kiri'/left); commonly used in directions and everyday navigation.

sentences.text: Belok kanan di lampu merah itu.
sentences.en: Turn right at that red light.

sentences.text: Toko itu ada di sebelah kanan.
sentences.en: The shop is on the right side.

sentences.text: Tangan kanan saya sakit hari ini.
sentences.en: My right hand hurts today.

note: "Kiri" means "left" (direction); often paired with "kanan" (right); used in directions and everyday navigation.

sentences.text: Belok kiri di lampu merah itu.
sentences.en: Turn left at that red light.

sentences.text: Tangan kiri saya sakit hari ini.
sentences.en: My left hand hurts today.

sentences.text: Tolong duduk di sebelah kiri saya.
sentences.en: Please sit on my left side.

note: "Kuning" means yellow; commonly used for colors of objects, fruits, and clothing; related words include "kuning telur" (egg yolk) and "kekuningan" (yellowish).

sentences.text: Baju saya berwarna kuning cerah.
sentences.en: My shirt is bright yellow.

sentences.text: Pisang itu sudah kuning dan manis.
sentences.en: That banana is already yellow and sweet.

sentences.text: Mobil kuning itu milik pak guru.
sentences.en: That yellow car belongs to the teacher.

english: then, after that, Then? Then what?, What happened then?
note: "Lalu" means "then" or "after that" in a sequence of events; also used alone as "Then? / And then?" to prompt someone to continue a story; do not confuse with "terus" which is nearly synonymous but more colloquial.

sentences.text: Saya makan nasi, lalu minum air.
sentences.en: I ate rice, then drank water.

sentences.text: Dia pergi ke pasar, lalu pulang.
sentences.en: She went to the market, then went home.

sentences.text: Kami mandi, lalu sarapan bersama.
sentences.en: We showered, then had breakfast together.

note: 'Langit' means 'the sky'; often paired with 'biru' (blue) or 'cerah' (clear); do not confuse with 'udara' (air/atmosphere).

sentences.text: Langit di Bali sangat biru hari ini.
sentences.en: The sky in Bali is very blue today.

sentences.text: Anak itu melihat langit malam.
sentences.en: That child is looking at the night sky.

sentences.text: Langit cerah, kita bisa pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: The sky is clear, we can go to the beach.

note: 'Merah' means red; commonly used in phrases like 'lampu merah' (traffic light/red light); adjectives follow the noun in Indonesian.

sentences.text: Baju saya berwarna merah.
sentences.en: My shirt is red.

sentences.text: Lampu merah itu berarti berhenti.
sentences.en: The red light means stop.

sentences.text: Dia suka bunga merah.
sentences.en: She likes red flowers.

note: 'Penting' means 'important'; commonly used in both formal and informal speech; related words include 'kepentingan' (importance/interest) and 'terpenting' (most important).

sentences.text: Belajar bahasa Indonesia sangat penting.
sentences.en: Learning Indonesian is very important.

sentences.text: Ini adalah dokumen yang penting.
sentences.en: This is an important document.

sentences.text: Kesehatan itu sangat penting bagi kita.
sentences.en: Health is very important for us.

note: 'Putih' means white or colourless; commonly used in everyday descriptions; related words include 'hitam' (black) and 'merah' (red).

sentences.text: Baju saya berwarna putih dan bersih.
sentences.en: My shirt is white and clean.

sentences.text: Kucing itu berbulu putih dan lucu.
sentences.en: That cat has white fur and is cute.

sentences.text: Nasi putih dimakan setiap hari.
sentences.en: White rice is eaten every day.

note: "Sebentar" means a short moment; often used in "tunggu sebentar" (wait a moment); don't confuse with "segera" (immediately/soon).

sentences.text: Tunggu sebentar, saya ambil uang dulu.
sentences.en: Wait a moment, I will get money first.

sentences.text: Saya mau istirahat sebentar di sini.
sentences.en: I want to rest for a moment here.

sentences.text: Dia pergi sebentar ke pasar.
sentences.en: She went to the market for a short time.

note: 'Tolong' means 'please' when asking for help; place it before a verb; do not confuse with 'silakan' which means 'please go ahead/help yourself'.

sentences.text: Tolong bawa air minum untuk saya.
sentences.en: Please bring drinking water for me.

sentences.text: Bisa tolong panggil dokter sekarang?
sentences.en: Can you please call a doctor now?

sentences.text: Tolong tutup pintu itu, ya.
sentences.en: Please close that door, okay.

english: the end (of an object, i.e. the furthermost, extremity of something)
note: "Ujung" refers to the tip or far end of a physical object (e.g. a finger, road, or stick); not used for time endings — use "akhir" for that.

sentences.text: Rumahku ada di ujung jalan ini.
sentences.en: My house is at the end of this road.

sentences.text: Pegang ujung tali itu dengan kuat.
sentences.en: Hold the end of that rope tightly.

sentences.text: Ada warung kecil di ujung desa.
sentences.en: There is a small stall at the end of the village.

note: 'Warna' means colour/color and is used in everyday speech; common related words include 'warna-warni' (colourful) and 'berwarna' (to be coloured).

sentences.text: Apa warna baju kamu?
sentences.en: What colour is your shirt?

sentences.text: Saya suka warna biru dan hijau.
sentences.en: I like the colours blue and green.

sentences.text: Warna bunga itu sangat cantik.
sentences.en: The colour of that flower is very beautiful.

note: "Air kelapa" literally means coconut water/juice; commonly ordered at warung or beach stalls, distinct from "santan" (coconut milk used in cooking).

sentences.text: Saya mau minum air kelapa segar.
sentences.en: I want to drink fresh coconut juice.

sentences.text: Air kelapa ini sangat enak dan manis.
sentences.en: This coconut juice is very delicious and sweet.

sentences.text: Berapa harga air kelapa di sini?
sentences.en: How much is coconut juice here?

note: 'Air putih' literally means 'white water' and refers to plain drinking water; don't confuse with 'air minum' (also drinking water) or 'air' alone (which just means water).

sentences.text: Saya mau minum air putih sekarang.
sentences.en: I want to drink water now.

sentences.text: Tolong beri saya air putih, terima kasih.
sentences.en: Please give me some water, thank you.

sentences.text: Di meja ada air putih dan teh.
sentences.en: On the table there is water and tea.

note: "Anjing" is the standard Indonesian word for dog; note it can also be used as a strong swear word in informal/street speech, so context matters.

sentences.text: Saya punya anjing yang sangat lucu.
sentences.en: I have a very cute dog.

sentences.text: Anjing itu makan di depan rumah.
sentences.en: The dog is eating in front of the house.

sentences.text: Anak-anak bermain dengan anjing kecil.
sentences.en: The children are playing with a small dog.

english: to put a question, to ask a question
note: 'Bertanya' is the formal/polite verb for asking a question; closely related to 'tanya' (the base word); slightly more formal than everyday 'nanya'

sentences.text: Saya ingin bertanya kepada guru saya.
sentences.en: I want to ask a question to my teacher.

sentences.text: Dia bertanya tentang harga di pasar.
sentences.en: She asks about the price at the market.

sentences.text: Boleh saya bertanya sebentar?
sentences.en: May I ask a question for a moment?

note: 'Burung' means 'bird' and is used in everyday speech; it is a neutral, common word suitable for all ages and registers.

sentences.text: Ada burung kecil di pohon itu.
sentences.en: There is a small bird in that tree.

sentences.text: Burung itu terbang ke langit biru.
sentences.en: The bird flies into the blue sky.

sentences.text: Saya suka melihat burung di taman.
sentences.en: I like watching birds in the park.

note: 'Di luar' means 'outside' or 'outdoors'; note 'di' is a location prefix, and the opposite is 'di dalam' (inside).

sentences.text: Anak-anak bermain di luar rumah.
sentences.en: The children are playing outside the house.

sentences.text: Cuacanya panas di luar hari ini.
sentences.en: The weather is hot outside today.

sentences.text: Sepeda saya ada di luar.
sentences.en: My bicycle is outside.

english: on the right, on the righthand side (of)
note: "Di sebelah kanan" means 'on the right side of' something; its pair is "di sebelah kiri" (on the left); used for giving directions or describing locations.

sentences.text: Warung itu di sebelah kanan jalan.
sentences.en: That small restaurant is on the right side of the road.

sentences.text: Kamar mandi ada di sebelah kanan.
sentences.en: The bathroom is on the right-hand side.

sentences.text: Toko itu di sebelah kanan hotel.
sentences.en: That shop is on the right side of the hotel.

english: on the left, on the lefthand side (of)
note: "Di sebelah kiri" means 'on the left side (of something)'; the opposite is "di sebelah kanan" (on the right); used for giving directions or describing locations.

sentences.text: Warung itu ada di sebelah kiri jalan.
sentences.en: That food stall is on the left side of the road.

sentences.text: Kamar mandi ada di sebelah kiri.
sentences.en: The bathroom is on the left side.

sentences.text: Toko oleh-oleh di sebelah kiri hotel.
sentences.en: The souvenir shop is on the left side of the hotel.

english: in the middle, in the very middle of
note: "di tengah-tengah" means 'in the very middle of' (people, places, or situations); more emphatic than "di tengah"; commonly used in both formal and informal speech.

sentences.text: Dia duduk di tengah-tengah teman-temannya.
sentences.en: She is sitting in the middle of her friends.

sentences.text: Pura itu ada di tengah-tengah desa.
sentences.en: The temple is in the middle of the village.

sentences.text: Anak itu berdiri di tengah-tengah pasar.
sentences.en: The child is standing in the middle of the market.

note: 'Garasi' is an everyday informal word for garage, borrowed from Dutch; commonly used for both parking and storage spaces at home.

sentences.text: Mobil saya ada di dalam garasi.
sentences.en: My car is inside the garage.

sentences.text: Garasi rumah kami sangat besar.
sentences.en: Our house's garage is very big.

sentences.text: Dia menyimpan sepeda di garasi.
sentences.en: He stores his bicycle in the garage.

note: "Guru" means teacher in Indonesian; used for school teachers and spiritual guides; related word: "murid" (student).

sentences.text: Guru saya sangat baik dan sabar.
sentences.en: My teacher is very kind and patient.

sentences.text: Ibu guru mengajar matematika di sekolah.
sentences.en: The teacher teaches math at school.

sentences.text: Saya suka belajar dengan guru itu.
sentences.en: I like studying with that teacher.

note: 'Kelapa' means coconut (the whole fruit/tree); 'santan' is coconut milk, a common related word; used in everyday food and drink contexts across Indonesia.

sentences.text: Saya minum air kelapa di pantai.
sentences.en: I drink coconut water at the beach.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli kelapa di pasar hari ini.
sentences.en: Mom buys a coconut at the market today.

sentences.text: Kelapa itu besar dan segar.
sentences.en: That coconut is big and fresh.

note: 'Luas' describes physical area/space (room, land, sea); don't confuse with 'lebar' (wide in one dimension) or 'besar' (big in general size).

sentences.text: Kamar ini sangat luas dan nyaman.
sentences.en: This room is very spacious and comfortable.

sentences.text: Pantai di Bali sangat luas.
sentences.en: The beach in Bali is very extensive.

sentences.text: Kebun itu luas sekali.
sentences.en: That garden is very big.

note: 'Mangga' means mango (the fruit); do not confuse with 'manga' (Japanese comics) or the polite invitation word 'monggo/silakan'.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan mangga setiap hari.
sentences.en: I like to eat mango every day.

sentences.text: Di pasar ada banyak mangga segar.
sentences.en: At the market there are many fresh mangoes.

sentences.text: Mangga ini manis sekali.
sentences.en: This mango is very sweet.

english: to have something, to own something
note: 'Mempunyai' is formal; in casual speech Indonesians often shorten it to 'punya'. Both mean 'to have/own something'.

sentences.text: Saya mempunyai satu kucing di rumah.
sentences.en: I have one cat at home.

sentences.text: Dia mempunyai sepeda baru yang bagus.
sentences.en: She has a nice new bicycle.

sentences.text: Kami mempunyai warung kecil di Bali.
sentences.en: We have a small food stall in Bali.

note: "O ya" is a casual interjection used to introduce something you just remembered, similar to "Oh, by the way" or "Oh, before I forget"; common in everyday informal speech.

sentences.text: O ya, kita harus beli air minum.
sentences.en: Oh, before I forget, we need to buy drinking water.

sentences.text: O ya, toko itu tutup hari ini.
sentences.en: Oh, by the way, that shop is closed today.

sentences.text: O ya, ibu minta tolong belikan sayur.
sentences.en: Oh, before I forget, Mom asked us to buy vegetables.

note: 'Pembantu' means household helper/servant; 'bantu' is the root verb meaning 'to help'; avoid confusing 'pembantu' with 'asisten' which is more formal.

sentences.text: Pembantu saya memasak nasi setiap hari.
sentences.en: My household helper cooks rice every day.

sentences.text: Ibu mencari pembantu baru minggu ini.
sentences.en: Mom is looking for a new household helper this week.

sentences.text: Pembantu itu membersihkan rumah kami.
sentences.en: That household helper cleans our house.

note: 'Tinggi' means both 'tall' (for people/objects) and 'high' (for prices, mountains); beginners often confuse it with 'besar' (big/large).

sentences.text: Pohon itu sangat tinggi di taman.
sentences.en: That tree is very tall in the park.

sentences.text: Gunung Agung sangat tinggi di Bali.
sentences.en: Mount Agung is very high in Bali.

sentences.text: Harga buah itu terlalu tinggi.
sentences.en: The price of that fruit is too high.

note: "Ayo" is informal/friendly, used to invite or urge someone to do something together; similar to "mari" but more casual and energetic.

sentences.text: Ayo makan bersama di warung ini!
sentences.en: Come on, let's eat together at this warung!

sentences.text: Ayo pergi ke pantai sekarang!
sentences.en: Come on, let's go to the beach now!

sentences.text: Ayo main bola di sini.
sentences.en: Come on, let's play ball here.

note: 'Berdiri' means to stand or to stand up; related words: 'duduk' (to sit), 'bangun' (to wake/rise); used in everyday commands and descriptions.

sentences.text: Tolong berdiri di sini sebentar.
sentences.en: Please stand here for a moment.

sentences.text: Anak itu berdiri di depan kelas.
sentences.en: That child stands in front of the class.

sentences.text: Saya berdiri karena tidak ada kursi.
sentences.en: I am standing because there is no chair.

note: 'Bertemu' means 'to meet' (someone); use 'bertemu dengan' to say 'meet with someone'; related: 'ketemu' (informal spoken form).

sentences.text: Saya bertemu teman saya di pasar.
sentences.en: I meet my friend at the market.

sentences.text: Kami bertemu guru di sekolah hari ini.
sentences.en: We meet the teacher at school today.

sentences.text: Dia ingin bertemu kamu besok.
sentences.en: She wants to meet you tomorrow.

note: "Dulu" meaning "first" expresses doing something before anything else; often confused with "pertama" (first in order/rank) — "dulu" implies priority or sequence in actions.

sentences.text: Cuci tangan dulu sebelum makan.
sentences.en: Wash your hands first before eating.

sentences.text: Duduk dulu, saya ambilkan minuman.
sentences.en: Sit down first, I will get you a drink.

sentences.text: Tunggu dulu, saya belum siap.
sentences.en: Wait first, I am not ready yet.

note: "Jawab" means "answer/reply"; used as a verb (menjawab) or in narration as "kata/jawab" meaning "so-and-so answered/said"; don't confuse with "tanya" (to ask).

sentences.text: "Ya, saya bisa," jawab Budi dengan senang.
sentences.en: "Yes, I can," Budi answered happily.

sentences.text: "Tidak tahu," jawab Sari pelan.
sentences.en: "I don't know," Sari answered quietly.

sentences.text: "Rumah saya di sini," jawab anak itu.
sentences.en: "My house is here," the child answered.

english: a word, ... said so-and-so (in a, narrative)
note: 'Kata' means 'word' as a noun (e.g., 'a new word') and also functions as a quotative marker meaning 'said/according to' in informal narration; related to 'berkata' (to speak/say).

sentences.text: Kata ibu, warung itu tutup hari ini.
sentences.en: According to mom, the warung is closed today.

sentences.text: Saya belajar satu kata baru setiap hari.
sentences.en: I learn one new word every day.

sentences.text: Apa arti kata ini dalam bahasa Indonesia?
sentences.en: What is the meaning of this word in Indonesian?

note: "Kepala desa" is a formal title for the elected leader of a village; often shortened to "kades" in informal speech; related: "kepala" (head/chief), "desa" (village).

sentences.text: Kepala desa tinggal di rumah besar.
sentences.en: The village head lives in a big house.

sentences.text: Kami bertemu kepala desa hari ini.
sentences.en: We met the village head today.

sentences.text: Kepala desa membantu warga setiap hari.
sentences.en: The village head helps the residents every day.

english: to run, to run away, to escape
note: 'Lari' means to run or run away; don't confuse with 'pergi' (to go/leave) — 'lari' implies speed or escape; related: 'berlari' (running, more formal).

sentences.text: Dia lari ke pantai setiap pagi.
sentences.en: He runs to the beach every morning.

sentences.text: Anak itu lari karena takut anjing.
sentences.en: That child runs away because he is afraid of the dog.

sentences.text: Ayo lari! Hujan datang sekarang.
sentences.en: Let's run! The rain is coming now.

note: 'Luar' means 'outside/exterior'; often used in phrases like 'di luar' (outside) or 'luar negeri' (abroad); do not confuse with 'keluar' (to go out).

sentences.text: Anak-anak bermain di luar rumah.
sentences.en: The children are playing outside the house.

sentences.text: Di luar sangat panas hari ini.
sentences.en: It is very hot outside today.

english: to see something/someone, to look at
note: "Melihat" is the formal/written form; in casual speech "lihat" is used alone (e.g. "Lihat itu!"); not to be confused with "menonton" which means to watch (TV/a show).

sentences.text: Saya melihat pantai yang indah hari ini.
sentences.en: I see a beautiful beach today.

sentences.text: Dia melihat burung di pohon itu.
sentences.en: She sees a bird in that tree.

sentences.text: Anak itu lihat kucing di jalan.
sentences.en: That child looks at a cat on the street.

note: 'Membuka' is the formal/written form; 'buka' is used in casual speech and commands (e.g. 'Buka pintunya!'); also seen in 'buka puasa' (break the fast).

sentences.text: Tolong buka pintu itu untuk saya.
sentences.en: Please open that door for me.

sentences.text: Dia membuka jendela setiap pagi hari.
sentences.en: She opens the window every morning.

sentences.text: Ayo buka tasmu di sini.
sentences.en: Come on, open your bag here.

note: 'Mungkin' expresses possibility or uncertainty; it can function as an adverb ('maybe') or adjective ('possible'), and is used in both formal and informal speech.

sentences.text: Mungkin hari ini akan hujan.
sentences.en: Maybe it will rain today.

sentences.text: Dia mungkin ada di rumah sekarang.
sentences.en: She is maybe at home now.

sentences.text: Apakah itu mungkin untuk kita?
sentences.en: Is that possible for us?

note: 'Pakaian' is a neutral, everyday word for clothing/clothes; 'baju' refers more specifically to a shirt or top, while 'pakaian' covers all garments.

sentences.text: Saya membeli pakaian baru di pasar.
sentences.en: I am buying new clothes at the market.

sentences.text: Pakaian ini sangat murah dan bagus.
sentences.en: These clothes are very cheap and nice.

sentences.text: Dia mencuci pakaian setiap hari Minggu.
sentences.en: She washes clothes every Sunday.

note: "Panggung" means a raised stage or platform; commonly used for performances and events; related words: "pertunjukan" (performance), "penonton" (audience).

sentences.text: Penyanyi itu naik ke atas panggung.
sentences.en: The singer goes up onto the stage.

sentences.text: Panggung itu besar dan indah.
sentences.en: The stage is big and beautiful.

sentences.text: Anak-anak menari di panggung sekolah.
sentences.en: The children dance on the school stage.

english: to summon someone, to call out to someone
note: "Memanggil" is the active verb form of "panggil"; use it when calling out to someone by name or beckoning them — not for phone calls (use "menelepon" for that).

sentences.text: Ibu memanggil nama saya dari dapur.
sentences.en: Mom calls out my name from the kitchen.

sentences.text: Guru memanggil semua murid ke kelas.
sentences.en: The teacher summons all students to the classroom.

sentences.text: Saya memanggil teman saya di jalan.
sentences.en: I call out to my friend on the street.

note: 'Peraga' can mean a character in a story or play; note that 'karakter' is also commonly used, while 'peraga' may also mean 'model/demonstrator' in other contexts.

sentences.text: Saya suka peraga utama di cerita ini.
sentences.en: I like the main character in this story.

sentences.text: Peraga itu baik dan suka membantu.
sentences.en: That character is kind and likes to help.

note: "Sekeliling" means 'all around/surrounding'; often interchangeable with "sekitar", but "sekeliling" emphasizes encircling something completely.

sentences.text: Ada pohon di sekeliling rumah itu.
sentences.en: There are trees all around that house.

sentences.text: Anak-anak berlari sekeliling taman.
sentences.en: The children run around the park.

sentences.text: Saya melihat sawah di sekeliling desa.
sentences.en: I see rice fields all around the village.

note: 'Seperti' means 'like' or 'similar to' when comparing things; do not confuse with 'suka' (to like/enjoy).

sentences.text: Langit itu biru seperti laut.
sentences.en: The sky is blue like the sea.

sentences.text: Dia berlari seperti angin.
sentences.en: He runs like the wind.

sentences.text: Kue ini manis seperti madu.
sentences.en: This cake is sweet like honey.

note: 'Tadi' refers to something that happened earlier the same day or just a moment ago; don't confuse with 'kemarin' (yesterday) or 'sebelumnya' (previously/before).

sentences.text: Saya makan nasi tadi pagi.
sentences.en: I ate rice earlier this morning.

sentences.text: Dia telepon saya tadi.
sentences.en: She called me just now.

sentences.text: Tadi saya lihat kucing di sini.
sentences.en: Just now I saw a cat here.

note: "Tanya" means to ask a question; used in conversation and storytelling (e.g., "tanya Budi" = "Budi asked"); related words: "bertanya" (more formal), "pertanyaan" (question).

sentences.text: Dia tanya nama saya.
sentences.en: He asked my name.

sentences.text: Saya tanya harga nasi goreng ini.
sentences.en: I asked the price of this fried rice.

sentences.text: Ibu tanya di mana toilet.
sentences.en: Mom asked where the toilet is.

note: 'tiba-tiba' means 'suddenly/all of a sudden'; used in informal and formal speech; related to 'tiba' (to arrive); do not confuse with 'segera' (immediately/soon).

sentences.text: Tiba-tiba hujan turun sangat deras.
sentences.en: Suddenly it rained very heavily.

sentences.text: Kucing itu tiba-tiba lari ke jalan.
sentences.en: The cat suddenly ran into the street.

sentences.text: Teman saya tiba-tiba datang ke rumah.
sentences.en: My friend suddenly came to the house.

note: "Tidak usah" is informal/neutral and means there is no need to do something; similar to "tidak perlu" but more casual and common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Tidak usah membawa uang banyak ke sini.
sentences.en: You don't need to bring a lot of money here.

sentences.text: Tidak usah malu, semua orang belajar.
sentences.en: Don't be shy, everyone is learning.

sentences.text: Tidak usah masak, kita makan di luar.
sentences.en: Don't bother cooking, we'll eat out.

english: to take one's leave of, to ask permission to leave
note: "Minta diri" is a polite, slightly formal phrase used when excusing yourself before leaving; common in social and family settings, similar to saying 'I'll take my leave now'.

sentences.text: Saya minta diri dulu, sudah malam.
sentences.en: I'll take my leave now, it's already late.

sentences.text: Dia minta diri kepada tuan rumah.
sentences.en: He took his leave of the host.

sentences.text: Kami minta diri sebelum hujan turun.
sentences.en: We took our leave before the rain fell.

note: 'Pegawai' means employee or office worker; 'karyawan' is a common synonym, while 'pegawai negeri' specifically means government civil servant.

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah pegawai di kantor itu.
sentences.en: My father is an employee at that office.

sentences.text: Pegawai itu bekerja setiap hari.
sentences.en: That employee works every day.

sentences.text: Ibu saya seorang pegawai bank.
sentences.en: My mother is a bank employee.
